title: Evaluation of a wired tableau group
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $c$ be a binary code for its optional states, let $K$ be a template kind, let $m,s,t,p$ be natural numbers, and let $a$ be a Boolean assignment on natural numbers. The wired clause group evaluates to true under $a$ exactly when the corresponding bit-level template condition holds: its source block is read from time $s$, its target block from time $t$, and the selected input bit from index $p$, with the required equality or acceptance condition determined by $K$.
hypotheses_covered: A finite Turing machine $M$ over the binary alphabet
A binary code for its optional states
A Boolean assignment on natural numbers
replaced: For every source machine, state code, template kind, wiring data, and assignment $a$, the wired clause group evaluates to true under $a$ exactly when the bit-level meaning of the template holds: the wiring exposes the raw source and target blocks and the selected input bit exactly, so satisfaction means bitwise equations, never merely equality of decoded snapshots.
